note:
v1, IN THE TIME OF (track nine, whole-song skeleton). The drum pulse never leaves 84. Two guitars teach seven strokes slowly: open F, mute, mute, answer, mute, answer, mute. Each seven bars the space between strokes shrinks: one per beat, then two, three, four, five and six. Before seven, the head of the cell meets a quarter only once in seven beats. The two pitch answers alternate; the articulation repeats in seven strokes, the pitches in fourteen.
At five and six (1:20–2:00) the guitars thin to two and a short F4 tap marks each cell head. Its two custom wavetable frames come from the riff: harmonics 1/4/6 from the open notes, 2/3/5/7 from the muted ones. At 2:00 the tap gives its job to the kick and bass: seven guitar strokes now fit one quarter, six guitars play them, and the rhythm section walks. At 2:40 the slow seven strokes return as chords. 3:06 written, 3:11 with the tail.
LISTEN FOR:
- the opening cell, one stroke per beat: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v1-cell.mp3
- six into seven (1:55): the kit alone for one beat; the cell locks to the kick: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v1-lock.mp3
- seven back to one (2:36): the opening played as chords: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v1-return.mp3
- the cell-head tap at five then six strokes per beat (1:35): http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v1-tap.mp3
- full song: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v1-full.mp3
WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): 81.27 / 82.24 on seeds 0 / 11. Both files −10.0 LUFS, −1.29 dBTP. At the lock the band steps up 2.0 LU, against 0.5 in the first draft. I cut the kick from all 392 fast strokes to the 56 cell heads (checked against the guitar timestamps). The mono mix in the first three bars of the lock is 2.7 dB short at 60–120 Hz and 2.9 over at 120–250 vs the reference records. I kept the quarter-note kick rather than putting the roll back for low end. The tap at −9 dB gain sits 8.4 / 8.9 dB under the stereo mix on its attacks in the samples at 1:30 / 1:40; its first level put it over 11 dB under. The score's off-grid share reads zero despite the checked note grid; that measures the mixed accents, not the written spacing.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the kit lets you feel the same beat at every speed; whether the landing feels heavier or just busier; whether you recognise the opening when it comes back. No new card: the existing listening page can be answered in its own time.
NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

note:
v2, PICKED AND KEYED (palette round as drawn, 1:00–1:20). At four notes to the beat the seven-stroke riff has two pitches trying to speak between the low F strokes. In v1 four distorted guitars played both pitches together. Here the guitars leave those two places empty: a baritone guitar on the left picks the first note an octave up; a clavinet on the right keys the other, two octaves up. Eight cells later, at 1:10, they swap who asks and who answers. Their sides do not swap. The bass keeps the original pitches; the kick, snare and cell heads stay where they were. At 1:20 the pair stops and the existing tap marks the fives. Nothing added to the 2:00 lock.
LISTEN FOR:
- Same nine seconds around the handoff (1:07), v1 then v2: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v2-before-after.mp3
- The exchange in context (0:56 through 1:22), from threes to fours to fives: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v2-hands.mp3
- Full song: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v2-full.mp3
WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): 32 written hook times, 16 taken by each player. Every other track besides the four affected guitars is note-identical to v1; the only edits to those guitars are at the 32 hook times. In the first bench the baritone dominated: its first 100 ms sat just 1.1–1.4 dB under the stereo K-weighted raw mix (medians per half), against 6.1–6.2 for the clavinet. Kept levels put the picked attacks 4.9/5.5 dB under, the keyed ones 5.9/5.8 under. Average mix image over the whole file: 0.1 dB right on seed 0. The cost is a lighter rung: the finished section reads −10.3 LUFS instead of −9.6. In the mono sum all nine band shares in that stretch are within 1.2 dB of the eleven-record median. Compscore 81.42/82.51 (v1 81.27/82.24); both renders −10.0 LUFS, −1.29 dBTP. I kept it for the exchange, not the score.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the two players sound like one riff changing hands, or two interruptions; whether the lighter twenty seconds set up the five-stroke section or take too much weight off the guitars. No listening card was pending on this track; no card added or clip replaced.
NOT HEARD BY ANYONE.

note:
v3, THE TWO WHO STARTED IT (whole song: statement and return). At 0:10 the right guitarist lets the two answer pitches ring an octave up across the left hand's next muted F. At 2:40 the slow seven strokes return: two guitars hold those upper answers and the inside pair plays the clipped pedal. On the third cell the inside pair leaves the pedal and takes the answers another octave up. At 2:55 four players drop out: the opening's two guitar parts at 0:15 come back note-for-note over the band. All six hit the existing F at 3:00. No new tune, instrument, bar or tempo change. Every note from 0:20 to 2:40, every non-guitar part and the final chord are unchanged. C10T9_RING='' gives v2 byte-for-byte.
LISTEN FOR: does hearing just the two guitars again give the last F somewhere to land? The last change, v2 then v3: http://pocket4:8790/clips/three-c10-t9-v3-return-ab.mp3 . The same duet at 0:15: http://pocket4:8790/clips/three-c10-t9-v3-opening.mp3 . Not checked by ear.
Same-neighbour, whole-song seeds 0/11: 81.42/82.51 -> 82.18/82.65. Both -10.0 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. Each of the four returning cells had 42 written guitar attacks; now 28, 28, 22, 12. The last five seconds before the F measure -11.76/-11.59 LUFS; the first four seconds of the F -8.59/-8.55. A 3.2/3.0 LU landing, versus 0.8/0.7 in v2. An arrangement decision, not a louder master; quieting that last cell could also feel like losing weight. The 84 BPM kick at the lock and the picked/keyed exchange are intact.
next: Listen to the bookend card it-return-duet before changing the opening or the last four cells again. If interested in the next untouched rung, try giving the drummer a three-against-four response at 0:40 rather than adding to the keyed fours or the 84 BPM lock.

note:
v4, FOUR UNDER THREE (section round, window 3). The guitars are still playing triplets, but the drummer starts grouping them in fours a few bars before the band changes speed. From 0:45.7 to 1:00 the foot closes the hi-hat on four quarters while the sticks mark every fourth guitar stroke: three accents per bar against four foot taps. For two bars the ride bell has all three and the snare keeps the familiar backbeat. Then bell–snare–snare, snare–bell–snare, and finally the snare plays all three, rising in strength. At 1:00 the ordinary backbeat returns under four guitar strokes per beat. No new guitar line, no change of tempo. The kick, bass and the seven-note cell are untouched throughout.
LISTEN FOR:
- Pedal hi-hat, ride bell and snare on their own, then the same five bars with the band: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v4-foot-and-sticks.mp3
- Same passage from 0:48, v3 then v4. Listen for the snare taking the ride bell’s three before the backbeat returns: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v4-before-after.mp3
- Full song: http://pocket4:8790/clips/chirper-zero-inthetimeof-v4-full.mp3
WHAT I MEASURED (I cannot listen): 20 foot taps and 15 cross-accents (8 ride bell, 7 snare), plus the four backbeats in the first two bars. The first bench left the foot almost 15 dB below the raw mix in those two bars. At the kept levels the median first 100 ms of the foot and bell are 9.3/6.8 dB below the stereo K-weighted mix; after the backbeat moves, snare attacks are 3.1 dB below it. The price is a little more top: 8–16 kHz gains 1.5 dB relative to v3 in those first two bars, now 0.3 dB over the eleven-record median. The completed passage is within 0.1 LU of v3 on each side of the change of hands. The only window marked by the audio comparison is w3 (−11.0 dB residual; all others −81.4 dB or lower, including opening and ending).
Seed 0 / 11: 82.14 / 82.66; v3 published at 82.18 / 82.65. Keep for the drummer’s three against four, not the score. Both full renders −10.0 LUFS, −1.29 dBTP. The isolated groove in the first clip is rendered as three tracks through the same buses, without the kick, with the raw-to-mastered full-band gain for that passage; it is not the sum of three individually mastered stems.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the foot is clear enough to count four under the stronger snare, or whether the last bar sounds like a fill that starts too early. The v3 opening/ending card it-return-duet is still waiting: neither passage was edited and its clips were not replaced. No new card.
